title: The Wind and the Sun

sentences.text: The wind and the sun argued about who was stronger.
They saw a traveler walking the road in a thick cloak.
Whoever can make that traveler take off the cloak is stronger, said the sun.
The wind went first and blew with all his might.
Dust flew, branches bent, and the traveler grabbed the cloak tighter.
Then the sun took a turn and shone, gentle and warm.
The road heated up, and the traveler wiped his brow.
He loosened the cloak, then took it off and folded it over his arm.
The sun had won without a shout. Warmth had worked better than force.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A traveler who sews a brand-new cloak
A storm that knocks down every tree
The sun and wind taking a long nap

questions.explanation: The wind blows hard and the traveler holds on tighter. The warm sun gets the cloak removed. The story is about a gentler way winning.

questions.prompt: What does the traveler do when the wind blows hard?

choices.text: He folds the cloak over his arm
He asks the sun for a race
He drops the cloak in the dust

questions.explanation: The story says that when the wind blew, the traveler grabbed the cloak and held it tighter. Taking it off happens later, in the sunshine.

choices.text: The wind and the sun start to argue
The wind blows with all his might
The traveler folds the cloak over his arm
The sun begins to shine warmly

questions.explanation: The argument comes first, then the wind, then the sunshine. The last action is the traveler removing the cloak and folding it.

attribution: A retelling of a public-domain fable by Aesop. The wording is original.
